reasoning: The two failures are 5000ms test-runner timeouts (not assertion failures). The application implements the spec goals: static/media/view.js wires initializeFaceTapHighlighting (a click/tap handler that calls clearHighlights() then highlightFace(faceId), which strokes #faceCanvas and adds .highlighted) and updateCanvasSize redraws the remembered highlightedFaceId on resize, so both 'tap draws the box' and 'resize redraws instead of losing it' are achievable. routes/media.py only passes faces_with_locations for faces that have location data, so highlightFace can actually paint. The same file's passing test photo_details_metadata_actions_are_touch_sized uses the identical withTouchContext + findFirstPhotoIdWithDetectedFaces + page.goto setup and finishes in 506ms; it does NOT waitForFaceCanvas/tap/read canvas pixels, which isolates the extra cost to the face-highlight path. The only two tests that combine a fresh mobile context (isMobile+hasTouch), a ~2MB full-res image load, waitForFaceCanvas, getImageData canvas reads, tap-with-scroll-into-view, and (for the rotation case) a resize + expect.poll are the ones that exhaust the aggressive default 5000ms budget. The sibling face_assignment responsive spec that uses the same withTouchContext + tap pattern explicitly raises the budget with test.describe.configure({ timeout: 90_000 }); this spec does not. The tests previously passed (progress notes record 15/15 for the photo_details family), so this is a timeout-budget/robustness defect in the test code, not an app regression.
affectedTests: Photo Details - Responsive › photo_details_face_highlight_works_with_a_coarse_pointer - tapping a face draws its box
Photo Details - Responsive › photo_details_face_highlight_survives_rotation - resizing redraws the box instead of losing it
suggestedAction: Raise the timeout for the touch-context cases in photo-details-responsive.spec.ts (e.g. test.describe.configure({ timeout: 30_000 }) or per-test test.setTimeout(30_000)), and give waitForFaceCanvas and the expect.poll explicit timeouts so a genuine failure surfaces as a clear assertion error instead of a bare test timeout. Keep the app untouched.
